subject: MAP & SLA tradeoffs — Acme Health evaluation plan and pricing milestones
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Bennett <olivia.b@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Liu <david.liu@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP + eval plan for Acme — timeline and example SLAs

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on the telemetry workloads and clinical latency sensitivity. I promised a concise mutual action plan (MAP) + evaluation plan to align timing, deliverables, and commercial milestones. Attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP_Acme_v1.pdf) that ties evaluation gates to incremental pricing/commit ramps.

High level:
- Week 0–2: Sandbox ingestion + baseline perf run (no cost to you).
- Week 3–4: Pilot eval with production-ish traffic (SLO measurement window).
- Week 5–8: Canary rollout + stability run — successful canary unlocks ramped committed capacity and discount.

We propose commercial checkpoints: a provisional 15% pilot discount, increasing to a 25% committed discount once the canary meets the agreed latency SLOs for two consecutive 7-day windows. If the canary misses the SLOs, we hold discount and loop in engineering to remediate (we’ll include an escalation cadence in the MAP).

Two asks from procurement/ops teams I want to surface now so we can close faster:
1) Is Acme comfortable with latency SLOs defined as p95 end-to-end inference latency (measured at your egress) with a 7-day measurement window?
2) Is procurement looking for a formal credit-based SLA or prefer a contractual remediation plan (engineering fixes + extended trial)?

I’ve attached the draft MAP and an SLA appendix with example credit language. Can you confirm who from Acme should be on the 1:1 weekly MAP sync and procurement leads we should include on the DocuSign / legal thread?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_Acme_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Olivia Bennett <olivia.b@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Liu <david.liu@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + eval plan for Acme — timeline and example SLAs

Thanks Vanessa — this looks aligned with what we discussed. A few quick notes:

- We can do p95 as the starting metric but clinical ops will push for a hard p99 target for certain flows (patient lookup). Can we show both buckets in the MAP?
- Procurement prefers explicit credit language in the SLA; they want a cap and an easy calculation. Their bigger ask is limit our operational risk (i.e., they want credits instead of engineering-only remediation).
- Legal will want a maximum annual uptime / latency credit cap and clearer definitions of measurement points and excluded outages (e.g., planned maintenance).

People to include on the weekly sync:
- Olivia Bennett (Clinical Ops)
- David Liu (IT Architect)
- Hannah from Procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com)

If you can revise the MAP to include p95/p99 tiers and a draft credit table, I’ll push this to procurement/legal for a light review.

-Olivia

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Bennett <olivia.b@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Liu <david.liu@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + eval plan for Acme — timeline and example SLAs

Olivia — thanks, that’s helpful. I’ve updated the MAP to include p95 and p99 tiers and a simple credit table (see attached MAP_Acme_v2.pdf and SLA_appendix_redwood.pdf). Key changes:

- SLO definitions: p95 <= 120ms (target), p99 <= 250ms (safety tier). Measurement is at your egress, with Redwood providing the observed metrics and a shared dashboard.
- Credit table (proposal):
  - If p95 breaches target for a 7-day window: 5% monthly credit (applied to next invoice), capped at 15% per quarter.
  - If p99 breaches safety tier for a 7-day window: 10% monthly credit, capped at 25% per quarter.
  - Credits only trigger on sustained windows (>=72 hours of degraded state) and exclude scheduled maintenance with 48-hour notice.

Commercial linkage to MAP milestones:
- Pilot success (meets p95 target for one 7-day window): pilot discount (15%) converts to trial committed rate and unlocks 50% of proposed committed capacity.
- Canary success (two consecutive 7-day windows meeting p95): full committed discount (25%) and ramp to 100% committed capacity per MAP timeline.

Engineering note: to meet p99 for certain patient-lookup flows we recommend pinning an optimized model variant and enabling local KV caching on the pipeline. I’ve looped Aditya (cc’d on the next message) for feasibility/cost estimates — this may affect committed capacity pricing.

If procurement/legal are okay with the credit caps and exclusion language, we can propose this as the final SLA appendix for DocuSign. I’ll also prepare a short mutual action checklist for the weekly sync.

Best,
Vanessa

Attachments: MAP_Acme_v2.pdf (application/pdf), SLA_appendix_redwood.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 14:25:00 -0800
Subject: Internal — Acme MAP / proposed SLA credits and exposure

Team — looping you in so we can finalize the commercial ask. Quick summary of what's on the table with Acme:

- MAP timeline: 8 weeks (sandbox -> pilot -> canary -> ramp)
- Proposed discounts: 15% pilot -> 25% committed upon canary success
- Proposed SLA credits (see attached): 5%/10% monthly credit triggers with quarterly caps (15%/25%)

Procurement will push for larger credit caps and may insist credits apply from day one of the production ramp. My recommendation is to keep a cap but offer an alternative: instead of large ongoing credits we can offer a temporary committed capacity discount or a bill credit that phases down as remediation progresses.

Questions for legal and sales ops:
1) Are the credit caps above acceptable from a legal perspective?
2) Can we limit credit applicability to sustained degradation windows (>=72 hours) and exclude documented third-party outages?
3) If we offer a temporary committed capacity discount, do we want that to be convertible into committed spend (i.e., counts toward the committed capacity in the contract)?

Aditya — can you add a rough cost delta for pinning the optimized variant + KV caching (2–4 GPU hours/day estimate) so we can show the impact on unit economics to Acme?

Thanks,
Vanessa

[Quoted earlier: updated MAP and SLA appendix attached]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal — Acme MAP / proposed SLA credits and exposure

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary. I’m comfortable moving forward with the approach but want to tighten the credit mechanics to reduce our exposure:

- Replace single-trigger credit with tiered windows: 72–168 hours degraded => 5% credit; 168–336 hours => 10% credit; >336 hours => escalate to executive review and apply up to 20% cap for the month (still bound by quarterly cap).
- Make credits payable only after remediation steps are logged and a joint postmortem is accepted — this prevents gaming and ties remediation to payment.
- Approve the alternative of a temporary committed capacity discount, but it must be explicitly convertible into committed spend (counts toward the 12-month commit) and time-bound (max 90 days).

Marissa — please confirm legal language changes (payable after postmortem + PM acceptance). Aditya — please send the cost estimate; if pinning an optimized variant materially increases cost we should show a blended committed rate.

If legal and eng sign off, Vanessa — propose we send this as the next update to Acme with the revised credit table and the alternative convert-to-commit discount. I’ll join the weekly sync.

- Rishi
